query: What signals are linked to longer resolution duration values?

per_column.name: duration_category
per_column.rationale: Binning the resolution duration into short/medium/long is a direct discretization of the focus variable itself, not an external predictor.

per_column.name: is_critical
per_column.rationale: A criticality/priority flag is an independent attribute known at ticket intake and plausibly correlates with resolution duration without restating it.

per_column.name: duration_minutes
per_column.rationale: This is the resolution duration expressed in minutes -- a deterministic unit transform of the focus variable, hence a restatement/leakage of the outcome.

per_column.name: has_db_issue
per_column.rationale: A flag derived from the ticket's short_description indicating a database-related problem is an external descriptive signal that could plausibly predict longer resolution times.

judge.rationale: Only two of the four added columns are legitimate external predictors (is_critical, has_db_issue); the other two (duration_category, duration_minutes) are direct restatements/transforms of the focus variable and constitute leakage. The valid predictors carry modest signal -- criticality is largely available from the existing priority column, so the incremental leverage beyond the original table is limited, with has_db_issue offering the most genuinely new signal derived from text.
